text:
incident-bot: Pager: PROD - VELA dedicated pool: intermittent 502/504s observed on tenant endpoints (vela-prod). Severity: P2. Affected: private VPC, NLB → targets failing healthchecks. See: https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-4732

emily: Acknowledged, taking it. Collecting telemetry now. @carla can you confirm customer-facing reports?

carla: Customer (lisa@vela) reports spike in errors since 02:12 UTC. ~3% of requests returned 502/504, some users seeing timeouts ~3-5s. They're asking for ETA.

dylan: Running quick checks on NLB/target groups + SG logs. Starting with `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...`

marco: I see a scheduled infra runbook executed at 02:10 that tightened an egress/inbound SG for the host fleet — looks like it removed a permissive rule that allowed NLB health IP ranges. Possible correlation.

sree: If healthchecks are blocked targets will be marked Unhealthy and traffic will route to fallback causing 502s. We should temporarily re-open SG to NLB healthcheck sources.

emily: @dylan please paste target health output and sample logs.

dylan: Paste: `TargetHealthDescriptions: [{Target: {Id: 'i-0abcde12345'}, HealthState: 'unhealthy', Reason: 'Failed health checks'}]`
NLB logs show repeated `connect_timeout` from NLB CIDR 34.198.0.0/16 to port 8080 on instances. SG was rejecting.

marco: Applying emergency rollback to add allow rules for NLB health IP ranges and health ports. Running: `terraform apply -target=aws_security_group_rule.allow_nlb_health` (starting)

emily: Customer comms: "We've identified a networking rule change impacting healthchecks and are applying a temporary whitelist. We'll follow up with a full RCA and timeline shortly." @lisa

lisa: Appreciate it. Our success rate dropped from 97% -> ~94% during the window. Users are seeing intermittent errors — please keep us posted.

ops-bot: terraform: apply completed in 18s — resources changed: 1 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed. Plan: add SG rule allow for NLB range and health port 8080.

dylan: Re-checking target health: now `Healthy`. `curl -I https://vela-prod.example.com/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` from NLB. Healthchecks pass.

sree: Suggest a durable fix: update scheduled runbook to skip SG tightening for customer-dedicated VPCs (tagged `customer:vela`). I'll prepare a PR to change the automation and add a preflight check against target groups.

emily: On-call handoff note: I'll leave detailed notes in #oncall. Handoff in 30m to night team. @carla please add this to customer post-incident pack: impact numbers, mitigation, and next steps.

carla: Acknowledged. Drafting postmortem and customer message. Will include timeline, peak error rate, and planned runbook change.

lisa: Thank you — we'd like a short meeting tomorrow to walk through the RCA.

marco: PR opened: `github.com/redwood/infra/pull/723` - change: skip SG tightening for workloads with `customer=vela` tag; adds unit test and preflight. Requesting review.

dylan: Marking incident resolved in ops dashboard (INC-2026-4732). Metrics: peak error rate 3.2%, affected window ~18m.

incident-bot: Incident update: severity downgraded to P3 and status: mitigated. Root cause: scheduled security group tightening blocked NLB healthchecks for dedicated customer VPC. Mitigation: emergency SG rollback applied, permanent runbook change pending. Links: https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-4732

emily: Closing thread once PR merged and postmortem published. Anything else?

marco: I'll follow up on CI and tests for the runbook change. Leaving a checklist in the PR.

carla: I'll send a customer-facing summary in ~1h and schedule the follow-up meeting.

lisa: OK, thanks everyone.
